surface: any /api/* path on the Kimi Code CLI local server (HTTP 401)
origin: code and HTTP status documented; the msg string is SYNTHETIC
notes: Unlike the success cases, this one does use a real non-200 HTTP status: authentication failure is one of the documented exceptions to the 'HTTP status is almost always 200' rule. Business code 40101. This is the state a QuotaVista connection lands in when the other tool's runtime is not logged in, or when its token was rotated - it maps to a needs-credentials state, not to a zero quota and not to an offline provider. Reading this endpoint at all requires a user-authorized connection flow; scanning for the token, importing browser cookies or reading another tool's credentials is forbidden by default. The msg text is invented. Every JSON response from this server is wrapped in {code, msg, data, request_id} and the HTTP status is almost always 200, so the business result is code (0 = success) and must be checked before data. Some error envelopes carry non-empty data, which is why checking the status line or the presence of data first is wrong. request_id is an invented 26-character ULID-shaped string. The server binds plain HTTP on loopback (127.0.0.1:58627 by default) and requires a bearer token for every /api/* path except the liveness probe; that token belongs to another tool's runtime and must never be captured, stored or committed. The whole API is documented as experimental: endpoints, fields and event types may change in any version, so the /openapi.json served by the version actually in use has to be re-validated at runtime before any of these shapes is trusted.
